candidate_theorem: Let W=D-kappa[psi] act on any finite bipartite space, kappa>=0, where D is real diagonal in a product basis and psi has Schmidt rank at most 4 and is supported on aligned basis pairs psi=sum_(i=1)^r c_i|ii>, r<=4. If W is nonnegative on every Schmidt-rank<=2 vector, then W is decomposable: W=A+B^Gamma for some A,B>=0. Thus no member of this whole aligned diagonal-minus-one-projector family can detect a PPT state. No equality of diagonal coefficients, matching symmetry, product-metric form, or full-rank assumption on D is made. This is one structured witness family only, not a solution of the unrestricted 4x4 PPT/SN3 problem. It is an UNREVIEWED WRITTEN CANDIDATE, not an adopted theorem.
normalization: 2-block positivity forces all diagonal coefficients of D to be nonnegative: for i!=j test |ij>, and for |ii> use <ii|W|ii>=d_ii-kappa|c_i|^2>=0. If kappa=0 or psi=0, W is PSD. If the Schmidt rank r<=3, restrict to the r x r local Schmidt support; this principal restriction remains 2-block positive, and is PSD for r<=2 or decomposable for r=3 by the known Yang-Leung-Tang theorem (https://arxiv.org/abs/1603.03534). All terms outside that local support are nonnegative diagonal, so lifting gives a global decomposition. For r=4, discard any outside-support positive diagonal terms, apply an invertible diagonal Bob congruence with entries 1/c_i, and divide by kappa. It suffices to prove W=sum_(i,j=0)^3 d_ij[|ij>]-[omega], omega=sum_i|ii>, with arbitrary d_ij>=0. Invertible local congruence preserves 2-block positivity and decomposability.
basic_inequalities: Put a_i=d_ii-1 and q_ij=sqrt(d_ij*d_ji). The 2-block-positive restriction to span{|ii>,|jj>} is [[a_i,-1],[-1,a_j]]>=0, so a_i>0 and a_i*a_j>=1 for every i!=j. For a perfect matching M={ij,kl} and any z_i>=0, a direct sum of two rank-one coefficient blocks with diagonal entries z_i,z_j and z_k,z_l gives, after optimizing offdiagonal entries, f_M(z)=sum_i a_i*z_i^2-2*sum_(i<j)z_i*z_j+2(q_ij*z_i*z_j+q_kl*z_k*z_l)>=0. Limits cover zero coefficients. The following fact is used repeatedly: a real symmetric matrix with offdiagonal entries <=0 is PSD if it is nonnegative on the nonnegative orthant, since x^T H x>=|x|^T H|x| for all real x.
graph_trichotomy: Form the graph G on {0,1,2,3} with edge ij whenever q_ij<=1. It is either disconnected, contains a perfect matching, or is a spanning star: in a connected four-vertex graph without disjoint edges, all edges pairwise intersect, so it is a star or triangle; a triangle is disconnected on four vertices.
disconnected_case: Every component C has size at most 3. For each cross-component pair, q_ij>1. Put B_ij=(1/q_ij)*[[d_ij,-q_ij],[-q_ij,d_ji]] on span{|ij>,|ji>}. This block is PSD, B_ij^Gamma cancels -|ii><jj|-|jj><ii|, and leaves nonnegative diagonal cross-pair terms. Each remaining component restriction W_C=sum_(i,j in C)d_ij[|ij>]-[sum_(i in C)|ii>] is 2-block positive and hence PSD when |C|<=2, or decomposable when |C|=3 by the imported theorem. Lift component decompositions and add the positive cross-pair remainders and B_ij^Gamma.
matching_case: If G contains matching M={ij,kl}, put B_ij=[[d_ij,-q_ij],[-q_ij,d_ji]] on each matched |ij>,|ji> block; this is PSD also when q_ij=0. All nonmatched offdiagonal-basis coefficients remain positive. The correlated block H of A=W-B^Gamma has diagonal a_i, offdiagonal q_ij-1<=0 on matched pairs and -1 on unmatched pairs. For all z>=0, z^T H z=f_M(z)>=0. Therefore H is PSD by the Z-matrix fact, and W=A+B^Gamma is decomposable.
star_setup: Let G be a spanning star with center 0. Thus q_0i<=1 and all leaf-pair q_ij>1. Set b_i=1-q_0i in [0,1], for leaves i=1,2,3. Define c_0i=q_0i and c_ij=min(q_ij,1+b_i*b_j/a_0) for leaf pairs. For q_ij>0 set B_ij=(c_ij/q_ij)*[[d_ij,-q_ij],[-q_ij,d_ji]], and set B_ij=0 if q_ij=0. Then B=sum B_ij>=0 and the offdiagonal-basis entries of A=W-B^Gamma are d_ij*(1-c_ij/q_ij)>=0, or d_ij when q_ij=0. The correlated block has center diagonal a_0, leaf diagonals a_i, center-leaf entries -b_i, and leaf-leaf entries min(q_ij-1,b_i*b_j/a_0). Its Schur complement at a_0 is the Z-matrix R with R_ii=r_i=a_i-b_i^2/a_0>=a_i-1/a_0>=0 and R_ij=-h_ij, h_ij=max(0,b_i*b_j/a_0-(q_ij-1)).
star_positivity: If every leaf q_ij>1+1/a_0, all h_ij=0 and R is PSD. Otherwise choose leaves j,k with q_jk<=1+1/a_0, and let i be the remaining leaf. Use matching M={0i,jk}. For nonnegative leaf z, choose z_0=(b_i*z_i+z_j+z_k)/a_0, which is nonnegative. The matching inequality f_M(z)>=0 becomes z^T C z>=0, where C_ii=r_i, C_jj=a_j-1/a_0, C_kk=a_k-1/a_0, C_ij=C_ik=-1-b_i/a_0, and C_jk=q_jk-1-1/a_0<=0. Thus C is copositive. All entries of R-C are nonnegative: this is immediate on the diagonal; for i,j and i,k use h_iell<=b_i*b_ell/a_0<=b_i/a_0; for j,k use h_jk=max(0,b_j*b_k/a_0-(q_jk-1)) and q_jk-1<=1/a_0. Consequently z^T R z>=z^T C z>=0 for all z>=0. Because R is a Z-matrix, R is PSD. The Schur complement then gives A>=0, so W=A+B^Gamma.

exact_example_check.observed: Fraction arithmetic checks one asymmetric-diagonal, non-PSD and non-coPSD 2-block-positive star instance: A and B are PSD of ranks 8 and 6; the matching Schur C and constructed Schur R are PSD; R-C is entrywise nonnegative; a star deficit is 1/20; W and W^Gamma have test values -7/5 and -1. This example's 2-block positivity follows in writing by adding a positive diagonal matrix to the earlier trace-inequality example. It is not a proof of the universal statement.

limits_and_dependencies: The only non-elementary import is the established 3x3 all-2-positive-maps-decomposable theorem. The general graph/matching/star proof is written and has not received disjoint scientific review, formal verification, or novelty clearance. It supersedes the owner's earlier uniform-diagonal, weighted matching and star-restriction candidates. Arbitrary nonaligned diagonal backgrounds, higher-Schmidt-rank negative kets, multiple negative projectors, and general 2-block-positive witnesses are not classified. No PPT/SN3 state or unrestricted 4x4 upper bound is claimed.
